summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of JusticeVerse. Backend 37/38 pytest passing (97%). Frontend critical flows verified: homepage, JusticeBot AI chat (Gemini reply with disclaimer rendered), Legal DB, Knowledge Hub, Careers, Pricing (Razorpay test plans), registration -> /dashboard redirect. Only one bug surfaced: brute-force lockout never triggers in the preview environment because client IP rotates across proxy nodes.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout fails to trigger. login_attempts identifier is `{request.client.host}:{email}`, but the K8s ingress sends requests from rotating proxy IPs (observed 10.208.130.77 / 10.208.130.78). Each proxy IP gets its own counter capped at ~3, so the 5-attempt threshold is never crossed for a single identifier; the 6th wrong attempt returns 401 instead of 429. Fix: trust `X-Forwarded-For` (or `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')`), or key purely on the email.

issues: GET /api/auth/me fires on every page and logs 401 to console for visitors. Not a functional bug, but spams the console. Consider suppressing or using a silent fetch.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout in /app/backend/auth.py login() — use X-Forwarded-For (first IP) or key identifier on email only so the 5-attempt threshold actually triggers behind the K8s ingress.
(Optional polish) Silence console 401 spam from AuthContext on unauth public pages.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py login(): brute-force identifier uses request.client.host which is a proxy IP in K8s -> lockout broken (see RCA).
routes_payments.py: rzp_client is created at import time with module-level env vars; if RAZORPAY_KEY_ID is missing the import fails silently. Consider lazy init + clear error.
routes_admin.py /admin/stats uses `async for` inside sum([...]) which evaluates the entire cursor in memory; fine for now but won't scale past a few thousand payments.
Frontend App.js: route is /database but the navbar label says LEGAL DATABASE. Naming inconsistency is acceptable but consider aliasing /legal-database for clarity / SEO.

auth.py google_session: stores raw session_token from Emergent and treats it as auth in _user_from_token. Works, but session_token is not signed by us; rotating Emergent's tokens would invalidate cookies. Acceptable for v1.
test_credentials: Admin admin@justiceverse.in / JusticeVerse@2026 verified (returns role=admin). Test users created on the fly via /api/auth/register (e.g. test_user_<rand>@example.com / TestPass@123).
seed_data_creation: Seed already populated by backend startup (8 legal docs, 3 articles, 4 news, 5 vacancies). Tests created TEST_-prefixed items via admin endpoints and cleaned them up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers all required endpoints — re-run with `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v`. After main agent fixes brute-force lockout, only the test_brute_force_lockout test needs to be re-verified. JusticeBot AI replies take ~10-25s, tests have 60s timeouts. Razorpay live checkout cannot be automated; only order-create + signature-mismatch are tested. Frontend nav routes are /, /justicebot, /database, /knowledge-hub, /careers, /pricing, /login, /register, /dashboard, /admin (do NOT use /legal-database — it doesn't exist).
rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout: identifier=`{request.client.host}:{email}`. In Kubernetes ingress the preview routes through multiple nginx/proxy pods, so request.client.host alternates between (at least) 10.208.130.77 and 10.208.130.78. After 6 wrong attempts from one client, attempts were split as count=3 on one identifier and count=3 on the other — neither hits >=5. Reproduce: `for i in $(seq 1 8); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"x@x","password":"wrong"}'; done` → all 401. Fix: use `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', '').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host` as the IP component, or drop IP and key only on email (simplest).
